property of the deal.

    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.

    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",

# Outcome sub-dossier — Costco Wholesale Corporation Mexico operation, realized ~3-5-year record

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written

> how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Outcome window (fixed at construction)
- The outcome is read from the company's Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended August 28,
  2016 (filed 2016-10-12), the annual report falling at the far edge of the fixed
  three-to-five-year window after the 2011 reference year. [SRC: SEC accession 0000909832-16-000032, Form 10-K (FY2016)]

## Public-reporting status (feasibility-relevant)
- The company remained a going concern filing annual reports throughout the window; the
  Mexico operation is reported as one of the countries in which it operates, consolidated
  within results rather than as a separate registrant. [SRC: SEC accession 0000909832-16-000032, Form 10-K (FY2016)]
- The selected financial data note records the accounting transition across the window:
  fiscal 2012 "Includes 50% of the results of Costco Mexico's operations in fiscal 2012
  prior to the July acquisition of our former joint venture partner's 50% equity interest.
  The remainder of fiscal 2012 and thereafter include 100% of Costco Mexico's results of
  operations." [SRC: SEC accession 0000909832-16-000032, Form 10-K (FY2016)]

## Realized record of the Mexico operation
- Retention and expansion, not divestiture: at August 28, 2016 the company operated 715
  warehouses worldwide, of which 36 were Mexico locations — an increase from the 32 Mexico
  warehouses reported at the 2011 reference date. [SRC: SEC accession 0000909832-16-000032, Form 10-K (FY2016)]
- Mexico is listed among the countries where the company is "principally engaged in the
  operation of membership warehouses" (U.S. and Puerto Rico, Canada, U.K., Mexico, Japan,
  Australia, Spain, plus majority-owned Taiwan and Korea), indicating the operation was
  retained as an ongoing consolidated business. [SRC: SEC accession 0000909832-16-000032, Form 10-K (FY2016)]
- The company operated 214 warehouses in eight countries outside the U.S. during 2016 and
  stated it planned "to continue expanding our international operations." [SRC: SEC accession 0000909832-16-000032, Form 10-K (FY2016)]
- Management continuity across the window: Dennis R. Zook is listed as Executive Vice
  President, Chief Operating Officer, Southwest Division and Mexico, an officer with the
  company since 1993, indicating the Mexico operation continued under the same divisional
  management structure. [SRC: SEC accession 0000909832-16-000032, Form 10-K (FY2016)]

## Documented disruption / impairment at the interfaces
- No asset-side impairment was recorded in the outcome year: "There were no impairment
  charges recognized in 2016," and long-lived-asset charges in prior comparative years
  were described as immaterial. [SRC: SEC accession 0000909832-16-000032, Form 10-K (FY2016)]
- The retrieved filing discloses no divestiture, closure, write-down, or restructuring
  specific to the Mexico operation over the window. [SRC: SEC accession 0000909832-16-000032, Form 10-K (FY2016)]

## Items noted but not primary-verifiable
- The FY2016 10-K reports foreign-currency and gasoline-price effects on net sales by
  country (including Mexico), but these are period-specific impact figures rather than a
  standalone Mexico segment result and are not recorded here as a Mexico outcome scalar.
  [UNVERIFIED: standalone Mexico net-sales or net-income scalar for the outcome window]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Within the fixed window the Mexico operation was retained and consolidated as a
  wholly-owned business, growing from 32 to 36 warehouses by August 28, 2016 while the
  company as a whole expanded to 715 warehouses; the company recorded no impairment charges
  in the outcome year and disclosed no divestiture, closure, or restructuring of the Mexico
  operation, which continued under the same divisional management. [SRC: SEC accession 0000909832-16-000032, Form 10-K (FY2016)]

[SLICE END]
